jobs.description:
HOW TO REACH US

- Bekim Krasniqi (Talent Acquisition), bekim.krasniqi@basf.com, Tel.:+49 30 2005-56136 will be happy to answer your questions for this position. You are also welcome to book an appointment online. Technical questions cannot be answered at this meeting.

WELCOME
If you're someone who inspires others, owns their impact and wants to elevate what they do, you'll fit right in.
Until July 1, our business was part of BASF. As part of the current transition, all job listings and the application process are still hosted on the BASF platform and therefore fully presented in BASF branding.
Please do not be confused by this: All roles are positions at Surventis, and your application will be submitted to us.
At Surventis, we go beyond the surface - in everything we do. We put customers at the center, think one step ahead, and develop solutions that create real value and lasting partnerships.
We inspire each other to think further, take ownership of our work, and constantly push to elevate what's possible. If you bring your full self, challenge the obvious answer, and want to grow with a team that means it - this is your place

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT
Due to the strategic realignment of the Coatings business unit, a dedicated accounting department is being established. This presents an exciting opportunity to develop and shape the finance organization from its foundation. Therefore, we are looking for a Global Functional Process Owner Book-to-Report / Record-to-Report (B2R) | Asset and Project Accounting with the following objectives:

- You own the global B2R | Asset- and Project Accounting Finance processes, which include the project accounting lifecycle from the initial financial evaluation until the execution of the financial project start-up and project closure, as well as asset accounting processes and lease accounting according to IFRS 16.
- You establish and maintain global standards for B2R | Asset- and Project Accounting processes, ensuring these are aligned with organizational goals and regulatory requirements across the coatings division.
- Moreover, you oversee the asset and project accounting activities, identify and drive process improvement opportunities, leveraging technology and digital solutions to enhance automation, efficiency, and continuous improvement within the finance organization.
- Furthermore, you manage a third-party business process provider in the area of Asset- and Project Accounting and implement process performance KPIs to steer the service provider.
- You collaborate closely with related functions such as project engineering, Purchase-to-Pay and General Ledger Accounting, you coordinate integration efforts and ensure holistic alignment of accounting processes.
- In addition, you engage with internal stakeholders to ensure that Asset- and Project Accounting processes meet business needs and support strategic objectives.

WHAT YOU OFFER

- university degree in finance, accounting, business administration, or a related field; additional certifications such as CMA or CPA are an advantage
- at least 10 years of work experience in financial process management and optimization, with a strong focus on Asset- and Project Accounting activities in a multinational corporation
- experience in the chemicals industry or a related industry, particularly during transitions or carve-outs, is highly beneficial
- strong understanding of accounting processes and process optimization methodologies
- proficiency in SAP R/3 and S/4, process mapping tools, and advanced MS Office skills
- excellent analytical, problem-solving, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to engage and influence diverse stakeholders in a multicultural environment
- fluency in English is required

WHAT WE OFFER

- We offer an attractive salary with individual benefits such as performance-related bonuses. Company-funded supplementary health insurance, accident insurance and pension related benefits.
- We offer a wide range of local and global development and career opportunities for professional and personal development.
- Surventis stands for diversity - we are proud of our Coatings employee networks WomenInCoatings, Color Pride and CultiConnect.
- The feedback culture is firmly integrated into our corporate culture, e.g. through regular employee surveys and management feedback.
- At our location in Münster, we have our own fitness studio "Freizeit" with a physiotherapy practice, permanently employed company doctors, a company restaurant "Auszeit" including a café bar, a bilingual company daycare center "LackiKids" and a vacation program "LackiKids on Tour".

BLISSAIR, based in Bocholt, Germany, is an aviation company, providing customized air transport solutions and aviation services.

BLISSAIR stands for safe, fast, and comfortable private air travel worldwide, delivered through our own aircraft fleet as well as an extensive network of partner aircraft.

Our facilities in Bocholt have recently been expanded to include a CAE Full-Flight Simulator for the King Air B200 equipped with a Pro Line 21 cockpit. A second simulator is already in the planning stage.

The simulator provides a highly realistic representation of the aircraft and is certified to the highest qualification standard, Level D. This gives BLISSAIR a unique market position, as it is the only simulator of its kind in Europe.

To support the ongoing maintenance and operation of this simulator, we are looking for an enthusiastic aviation-minded team player to join us as soon as possible.

Your Profile

- Completed vocational training as an Aircraft Electronics Technician, Electronics Technician, Mechatronics Technician, a comparable technical qualification, or a degree in an engineering or technical field.
- Good computer skills, particularly with Windows operating systems and older computer hardware
- Good IT skills, basic network setup and understanding of network protocols.
- Familiarity with technologies such as RS-232, Ethernet, Fibre Optics and Microcontrollers.
- Ability to repair and replace hardware components, perform soldering and rework, troubleshoot and diagnose electrical and electronic faults, trace wiring and signal paths, measure and test electrical circuits using diagnostic equipment, interpret electrical schematics, and carry out component-level repairs
- Ability to work independently with a high level of personal responsibility.
- Knowledge of C++ programming language and experience in the aviation industry are an advantage.
- Fluent in spoken and written english
- Quick learner with strong teamwork skills, initiative, and enthusiasm.
- Strong interest in technical systems and aviation industry

Your Responsibilities

- Work as part of the simulator maintenance team.
- Independently perform maintenance and servicing of simulator hardware, including quality checks.
- Provide technical support during customer training operations.
- Analyze and diagnose faults, carry out repairs.
- Document maintenance activities, inspections, and quality checks.

What We Offer

- A friendly working environment in a small team with an open, collaborative culture and flat hierarchies.
- A responsible and varied role with exciting technical challenges.
- The opportunity to work on a unique Level D King Air B200 simulator—the only one of its kind in Europe.
- A positive workplace atmosphere and modern facilities.
- The chance to contribute to internal process improvements and help plan and implement the company's second simulator.

Company Description

Conveying, loading, palletizing, packing, sorting and distributing - BEUMER Group develops and produces technically leading intralogistics systems for the global market. Our employees are characterized by excellent know-how and a strong will to consistently develop themselves further. We do our utmost to promote this claim: within the framework of a family-like cooperation characterized by high mutual esteem and a culture of trust that creates stability and security. Our common goal: to implement outstanding and innovative projects worldwide.

Job Description

In this role, you will take on a key position in further developing and shaping our evolving ServiceNow governance and platform landscape. Building on the existing framework and structures, you will actively contribute to enhancing processes, standards, and best practices to drive the platform’s continued maturity.

Your responsibilities include:

- Designing and implementing ServiceNow CSM and ITSM capabilities across core modules
- Developing flows, scripts, UI policies, IntegrationHub spokes, and upgrade‑safe customizations
- Building and managing integrations with external providers, including SLAs/OLAs, contracts, and vendor coordination
- Establishing and ensuring governance for release cycles, data models, error‑handling processes, and security boundaries
- Applying security best practices and maintaining documentation required for compliance and audits
- Working closely with Business Stakeholders to refine requirements and continuously enhance the platform
- Driving platform adoption through demos, knowledge articles, training sessions, and insights from performance analytics

Qualifications

- You hold a degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field
- Several years of hands‑on experience in developing ServiceNow solutions within ITSM and ideally also in CSM environments have shaped your expertise
- Communicating clearly, whether in documentation or in discussions with technical and non‑technical stakeholders, comes naturally to you
- Certifications such as CSA, CIS‑ITSM, or CIS‑CSM are a strong plus
- You work self-organized, analytical, and goal‑oriented in global virtual teams
- Curiosity and the drive to continuously learn and adapt in a fast‑changing environment define your working style
- You have strong English communication skills and beneficial German language skills that support effective collaboration in an international environment

Additional Information

We look forward to receiving your application! Please include your salary expectations (gross annual salary) and your notice period or earliest possible starting date.

Doctoral Position: Gene Expression Regulation (f/m/x)

Uhlirova Lab | Institute for Genetics | CECAD

We are one of the largest and oldest universities in Europe and one of the most important employers in our region. Our broad range of subjects, the dynamic development of our main research areas and our central location in Cologne make us attractive for students and researchers from around the world. We offer a wide range of career opportunities in science, technology, and administration.

The Uhlirova lab (www.uni-koeln.de/inter-fak/cecad/uhlirova/) explores how stress-inducible signaling pathways control gene expression and influence tissue homeostasis and longevity. To tackle these questions, we combine the power of functional genetics in Drosophila and mouse models with cutting-edge molecular and cell biology, multi-omics approaches, advanced microscopy, and bioinformatics. We are looking for a highly motivated and curious doctoral candidate (f/m/x) to join our dynamic team. You will have the opportunity to lead your own project, contribute to collaborative research, and develop skills at the interface of genetics, molecular and cell biology, and systems-level analysis.

The University of Cologne promotes equal opportunities and diversity. Women will be considered preferentially in accordance with the Equal Opportunities Act of North Rhine-Westphalia (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz - LGG NRW). We also expressly welcome applications from all suitable candidates regardless of their gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, disability, age, personal orientation and identity.

The position is available from immediately on a part-time basis (25,89 hours per week).The position is to be filled for three years. If the applicant meets the relevant wage requirements and personal qualifications, the salary is based on remuneration group 13 TV-L of the pay scale for the German public sector.

qualifications and the following documents:

A cover letter describing your motivation to join our research group and information on your career achievements (1 page max.)

To study the crosstalk between transcription and pre-mRNA splicing under physiological, stress, and disease conditions
To investigate mechanisms underlying spliceosome assembly and functional plasticity
To uncover what renders different transcripts, cells, and tissues sensitive to aberrant splicing
To investigate how spliceosome malfunction contributes to loss of tissue homeostasis, premature aging and diseases

Strong background in genetics, molecular and cell biology is essential

The Friedrich Schiller University Jena is a dynamic and innovation-driven university centrally located in Germany. With a broad range of disciplines, it shapes the future through excellent research and teaching. Its scientific excellence is reflected in the profile areas Light - Life - Liberty, which provide pioneering insights and sustainable solutions for the society of tomorrow. Through close collaborations with leading research institutions, innovative companies, and renowned cultural organizations, it advances interdisciplinary developments. With around 17,000 students and approximately 10,000 employees, it defines Jena as a vibrant, internationally connected city of science and innovation.

The Institute of Biodiversity, Ecology and Evolution at the Faculty of Biological Sciences seeks to fill the position of a

Doctoral Researcher in Viral Ecology (m/f/d)

commencing on 01 December 2026. We offer a part-time position (65%, 26 hours per week), with a fixed-term employment until 30 June 2030.

The DFG-funded Collaborative Research Centre 1768 “VirusREvolution: Decoding tools for virus research” is a highly ambitious research centre at Friedrich Schiller University with the joint goal to develop novel tools for virus discovery, characterisation, regulation, interaction, and visualisation (https://virusrevolution.uni-jena.de/). Its integrated research training group is educating doctoral researchers in a structured, interdisciplinary training program and invites applications for doctoral and postdoctoral researcher positions in various fields of research.
In this doctoral project “Do viruses exploit their quasispecies for host range evolution?”, you will investigate how host range and environmental conditions shape virus diversity and virus-host interactions in natural and experimentally manipulated microbial communities.
Conduct experimental work and analyses on virus-host interactions in soil and groundwater ecosystems, including host-range assays, environmental sampling, and targeted microcosm experiments
Analyse metagenomic and viromic data sets from soil and groundwater samples to identify broad- and narrow-host-range viruses to characterize their quasispecies characteristics
Participation in the Collaborative Research Centre VirusREvolution and close collaboration with the tandem project partner
Engage in regular discussions with other group and project members
Collaborate with BSc and MSc students working in associated projects
Publish papers and present your work at national and international scientific meetings

A highly motivated candidate with a Master of Science or equivalent degree in biology, microbiology, microbial ecology, virology, bioinformatics, or a related discipline
Experience in experimental microbiology, microbial ecology, and molecular biological methods; knowledge of sequencing-based bioinformatic approaches (metagenomics, viromics); experience with virus-host interactions are desirable.
Strong analytical thinking and problem-solving
Ability to work independently and in a collaborative team
Excellent skills in English are required, both written and spoken

Embedding in a cross-disciplinary, experienced research group and a large, ambitious research consortium
Affiliation to an Integrated Research Training Group, offering close support and a comprehensive education program for hard skills and transferable skills, supported by the Jena Graduate Academy
A family-friendly working environment with a variety of offers for families
University health promotion and a wide range of university sports activities
Remuneration based on the provisions of the Collective Agreement for the Public Sector of the Federal States (TV-L) up to salary scale E13 - depending on the candidate’s personal qualifications -, including a special annual payment in accordance with the collective agreement.
30 days of vacation per calendar year plus two days off on December 24 and 31

The Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy (MPI-SP) in Bochum is a research institute of the Max Planck Society for the Advancement of Science. It conducts interdisciplinary research on the diverse aspects of IT security and data protection. The newly established and expanding institute will ultimately comprise 18 research groups and employ around 200 staff members and guests. The institute cooperates with the Faculty of Computer Science at Ruhr University Bochum. Bochum is one of the world’s leading research locations for cybersecurity and is home to Europe’s largest training center in this field as well as a vibrant start-up scene.

Starting immediately, we are seeking a

Project Coordinator - AI Competition (d/f/m), 50%

to support the organization, communication, and implementation of an AI competition. The competition combines cutting-edge research in artificial intelligence and cybersecurity with the goal of advancing AI-based cybersecurity technologies. Teams from academia, start-ups, and industry will develop autonomous AI-based systems for identifying software vulnerabilities and assessing their exploitability.

Support communication and coordination with industry partners, policymakers, and other relevant stakeholders.
Project Coordination: Support meetings, schedules, documentation, reporting, and other organizational aspects of the project and ensure effective communication between the scientific team, project partners, participants, and external stakeholders.

We’re doing it with energy, curiosity and sheer dedication, always learning from unique perspectives of those around us, expanding our thinking, growing our capabilities and redefining ‘impossible’. There are so many reasons to join us. If you’re hungry to build a varied and meaningful career in a community of brilliant and diverse minds to make a real difference, there’s only one choice.

Senior Principal Scientist (all genders) - Quantum Mechanics and Modeling

As a key player in our R&D digital transformation, you will leverage quantum mechanics, physics-based modeling, machine learning and AI to predict molecular properties, design and prioritize compounds across our discovery portfolio. Collaborating closely with medicinal chemists, structural biologists, biologists, and data engineers, you will drive discovery project milestones and advance our digital transformation in R&D. Your role is crucial in shaping the future of drug discovery and development through innovative digital solutions.

- You advance drug discovery projects using quantum mechanics, data science, and modeling approaches to enable data‑driven decision‑making.
- You enable AI‑augmented Design‑Make‑Test‑Analyze cycles by advancing and applying methods for in‑silico compound design and characterization.
-

The Medical Faculty of Leipzig University, with its tradition spanning more than 600 years, is one of the largest research institutions in the Leipzig region. With over 1,300 employees, it is the largest of the university's 14 faculties and serves as a training center for approximately 3,500 students in human medicine, dentistry, pharmacy, and midwifery.

We are seeking a highly motivated Epidemiologist to design and conduct epidemiological research in pediatric populations, focusing on the determinants of child health, the development of common childhood diseases, particularly obesity, and the prevention and long-term outcomes of childhood obesity and metabolic diseases.
The research group "Childhood Obesity and Metabolic Research", led by Antje Körner, investigates the development, mechanisms and health consequences of childhood obesity. The translational approach combines experimental research, clinical studies and genetic approaches. We have large, well-characterized cohorts up and running with a longitudinal setting and across the entire age range: LIFE Child (n~6000), Leipzig Obesity Childhood Cohort (n~2500), and Leipzig Adipose Tissue Childhood cohort (n~700), with deep phenotyping allowing for combining clinical, epidemiological, lifestyle and functional omics and multi-omics data.

About the CRC 1774
The CRC 1774 investigates how key metabolic “promoter organs”-adipose tissue, bone marrow, the gut, and the liver-communicate with the cardiovascular system and thereby influence the progression from health through prediabetes and type 2 diabetes to cardiovascular diseases. By combining comprehensively characterized patient cohorts with state-of-the-art multi-omics technologies, innovative imaging techniques, and methods from data science and artificial intelligence, the project aims to decipher the mechanisms underlying cardiometabolic diseases and develop new approaches for precision medicine at the interface of diabetology and cardiology.

Doctoral students work on interdisciplinary research projects spanning basic, translational, and clinical research.
